thread:
maria: Quick sync — I found a few edge cases in the audit event vocab while validating customer-facing examples. We need to pick a stable naming convention before we ship the new schema to docs.

jon: ok, what are the gaps?

maria: Two main things: 1) delegated actions — we have both `delegation.create` and `user.delegation.create` used in different places; 2) KMS / BYOK events — some events include full key material identifiers and others only key aliases.

leo: +1 on standardizing. I prefer `service.resource.verb` (e.g., `kms.key.rotate`) so it's easy to filter by prefix.

sam: I worry about backwards compatibility. We already have customers relying on `delegation.create` in logs. Can we alias? :thinking_face:

ella: We should also decide on verb tense: past vs present vs noun-verb. Right now we have `key.rotated` and `key.rotate.requested` in the wild. That's confusing for alerting rules.

jon: Proposal: canonical form = `<product>.<resource>.<action>` with action in imperative (present) tense, e.g., `kms.key.rotate`, `auth.delegation.create`. Keep historical variants mapped in the ingestion layer for 6 months, then emit a deprecation header to customers.

maria: sounds reasonable. We'll need a migration plan for customer-facing docs + sample log outputs. Also need to call out PII redaction and KMS key identifiers.

sam: on KMS: we should never log raw key material or full ARNs with account IDs. Log stable key alias and a truncated identifier for debug (sha256 prefix). Example we can standardize on: `key_alias` + `key_fingerprint`. Eg: { "key_alias": "redwood-prod-1", "key_fingerprint": "sha256:3f4c...9a2b" }

maria: agreed. Add a `kms_provider` field (aws-kms, gcp-kms, hsm) and `key_reference_type: alias|fingerprint`. That helps RBAC and retention policies.

leo: RBAC side: audit events should include `actor` and `actor_roles` arrays so policy tools can reconcile who did what. Example (inline):
```json
{
  "event": "auth.delegation.create",
  "actor": { "id": "u_12345", "display_name": "maria" },
  "actor_roles": ["org_owner", "platform_admin"],
  "target": { "type": "delegation", "id": "d_9876" },
  "context": { "ip": "REDACTED", "user_agent": "REDACTED" },
  "version": "v1",
  "metadata": { "request_id": "r_abc123" }
}
```

jon: For customer-facing examples we must redact IPs and any user emails. Use `REDACTED` tokens and call out in the docs which fields may be redacted at export time.

maria: Also: vuln triage overlap — we found a vuln (VULN-1123) where audit logs didn't capture `role_change` actor details. We need a short-term patch to emit `auth.role.update` with the previous/next role in `metadata` for all role-change paths.

ella: Incident response note: When someone opens a customer incident, the playbook expects event names with `incident.*` prefix. Should we introduce `incident.audit.reference` as a stable pointer to related audit events?

leo: yes — `incident.audit.ref` or `incident.audit.link` pointing to an array of `request_id` or `event_ids`. That keeps incident tooling lightweight.

sam: audit ingestion: audit-bot (cc @audit-bot) can emit warnings when deprecated event names are observed in prod. audit-bot: can we add a linter rule for the event naming regex?

audit-bot: will do — proposing regex: `^[a-z0-9]+(\.[a-z0-9]+){1,4}\.(?:[a-z0-9_]+)$` and a maximum of 5 components. I will surface examples with suggested canonical replacements. :robot_face: 

maria: Great. Next steps: 1) create a short PR with the canonical naming rules and mapping table for deprecated names (sam to own), 2) add a temporary ingestion alias layer (eng-platform), 3) docs + customer-facing examples update (docs squad), 4) emit a communications plan for customers (support + account).

sam: I'll open the PR by end of day and add the mapping table. tagging @jon and @ella for review.

jon: I'll update the incident playbook to reference `incident.audit.ref` and ensure runbooks show redaction behavior.

ella: I'll coordinate with security-runbooks to include the `role_change` quick patch in the triage checklist.

leo: and I'll work with infra to make sure the ingestion alias layer can transform old events to new canonical names for 6 months.

maria: thanks all. If anyone has customer examples with odd names, drop them here and I'll include in the mapping PR. :thumbsup:

audit-bot: reminder: schema linter will start blocking on deprecated names next week (configurable by env).
